statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-85985 is MariaDB advisory GHSA-2245-9hm3-wxf6 (MDEV-40323): https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-2245-9hm3-wxf6 . The CONNECT storage engine's file-access UDFs json_file(), bson_file(), jfile_make(), bfile_make() and jbin_file() did not enforce the FILE privilege or the secure_file_priv setting, so a low-privileged user could read or write files the database account is not authorized to access, within operating-system permissions. MariaDB fixed it in 11.8.9 (and 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 12.3.3 and 13.0.2) with commit https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/4f66ca1b69daf1b7e6a562ca8e86d77a6a70abfe , which adds storage/connect/filechk.cpp with connect_can_access_file() and calls it from those UDFs in storage/connect/jsonudf.cpp and bsonudf.cpp. Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1 does not include it; Debian fixes trixie in 1:11.8.9+ds-0+deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-85985). DHI applies that commit's source changes unmodified, and the fixed version is the second build, the first that carries it. We compared all four published builds of Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1 in the DHI Debian repository (called the first to fourth build below; the fourth is the current build) on amd64 and arm64; each package we read was verified against the repository index checksum. In /usr/lib/mysql/plugin/ha_connect.so from mariadb-plugin-connect, the exported function connect_can_access_file and the warning text 'Access denied: FILE privilege or secure_file_priv violation' that the fix adds are absent in the first build and present in the second, third and fourth builds on both architectures, while the existing 'Missing file name' warning is present in all four. From the second build on, mariadb-test-data carries the upstream json_bson_file_priv regression test, and the shipped changelog lists this CVE.
